items.heading: Fixing a squeaky door hinge
precautionsFirst: Support the door if you remove it from its hinges for a heavier fix.
details: Apply a few drops of household oil, such as machine oil or even cooking oil in a pinch, or silicone spray, to the hinge pin.
Open and close the door a few times to work the oil in.
Wipe away any excess oil that drips out to avoid staining the floor.

items.heading: Fixing a loose door handle or knob
precautionsFirst: Support the handle assembly as you work so screws or parts do not fall and get lost.
details: Locate the small set screw on the neck of the handle, often needing an Allen key, and tighten it.
If the handle still wobbles, remove it fully, check the internal spindle for wear, and reseat it firmly before retightening.
Tighten the screws on the latch plate on the door edge as well, since these often loosen too.

items.heading: Fixing a door or window that sticks
precautionsFirst: Test gently before sanding or planing - only a small amount of material may need removing.
details: Identify where the door or window rubs by checking for shiny or worn marks along the frame.
Tighten any loose hinge screws first, since sagging hinges are a common cause.
If it still sticks, sand down the rubbing edge lightly with sandpaper, testing frequently.
Repaint or reseal the sanded edge to protect the wood from moisture.

items.heading: Patching a small hole or crack in a wall
precautionsFirst: Wear a dust mask when sanding filler, and ventilate the room.
details: Clean loose debris and dust from the hole or crack.
Apply a wall filler or putty with a scraper, slightly overfilling the hole.
Let it dry fully as per the product's instructions, then sand it smooth and flush with the wall.
Prime and paint to match the surrounding wall color.

items.heading: Touch-up painting a small wall area
precautionsFirst: Ensure good ventilation, and cover the floor and nearby furniture.
details: Clean the area to be painted and lightly sand any rough patches.
Use painter's tape to define clean edges if needed.
Apply primer if painting over a patched or stained area, and let it dry.
Apply the matching paint in thin, even coats, letting each coat dry before the next.

items.heading: Fixing a wobbly chair or table leg
precautionsFirst: Turn the furniture upside down on a padded surface to work on it safely.
details: Tighten any visible screws or bolts at the leg joints.
If a joint is loose from worn-out glue, apply wood glue into the joint, reassemble, and clamp tightly until dry.
For an uneven leg length, add a self-adhesive felt pad, or sand the longer leg slightly to level it.

items.heading: Fixing a torn window or door mosquito net
precautionsFirst: Work on a flat, stable surface if you remove the mesh frame.
details: For small tears, apply a mesh repair patch kit or a dab of clear or fabric glue, pressing the torn edges together.
For larger tears, cut a patch from spare mesh slightly larger than the hole, and glue or stitch it over the torn area.
For a fully worn-out net, most frames allow the old mesh to be pulled out and rerolled with new mesh sheeting from a hardware store.

items.heading: Unsticking a stuck zipper
precautionsFirst: Avoid forcing a stuck zipper, which can bend or break the teeth.
details: Rub a small amount of soap, candle wax, graphite pencil lead, or petroleum jelly along the teeth of the zipper.
Gently work the zipper pull back and forth to distribute the lubricant.
If fabric is caught in the teeth, gently wiggle it free with tweezers or a pin rather than pulling hard.

items.heading: Sharpening kitchen knives at home
precautionsFirst: Always cut and sharpen away from your body and fingers.
Keep fingers clear of the blade edge throughout.
details: Use a sharpening stone, or a simple pull-through sharpener suited for home use.
Hold the knife at the angle recommended by the sharpener, usually 15-20 degrees for a stone, and draw the blade across in smooth, even strokes.
Repeat evenly on both sides of the blade a few times.
Hone with a honing rod between sharpenings, and always wash the knife before use.

items.heading: Fixing a squeaky bed frame
precautionsFirst: Make sure the bed is stable and cannot collapse while you check underneath.
details: Tighten all visible bolts and screws at the joints with the appropriate tool.
Apply a little wood glue or wax to any wooden joints where a mattress slat rubs against the frame.
Place a folded piece of cloth or a felt pad between metal parts that rub against each other.

items.heading: Fixing a loose curtain rod or rail
precautionsFirst: Use a stable ladder or stool, and have someone hold it steady if working above head height.
details: Check if the wall bracket screws have loosened from the wall and tighten them.
If the wall anchor has come loose in the wall, remove it, fill the hole with wall filler, let it dry, and reinstall a slightly larger anchor.
Ensure the rod is level and balanced across both brackets before hanging the curtains back.
